jobs.title: Leukemia Specialist (193831)
jobs.institution: University of Rochester: Medicine: Hematology/Oncology
jobs.description:
The Department of Medicine, Hematology/Oncology Division and the Wilmot Cancer Institute are seeking a faculty that specializes in treating patients with Leukemia.
We are recruiting clinical researchers with a focus on contributing to a robust clinical trial portfolio supporting the Wilmot Cancer Institute's patient population and further scientific and clinical discoveries.
THE POSITION
The division is recruiting clinical researchers with a focus on contributing to a robust clinical trial portfolio supporting Wilmot Cancer Institute’s patient population and furthering scientific and clinical discovery. This will be achieved through a collaborative spirit of partnership with internal teams, including basic and translational scientists, clinicians and investigators, and other clinical and support staff. The ideal candidate will be expected to be a trusted colleague, clinician, investigator, and leader, and build productive relationships with teams across Wilmot, URMC, and UR Medicine, faculty, staff, residents, and fellows. Candidates will need to lead an active clinical practice, supporting clinical trial accruals and contributing to ongoing clinical and translational research, and ideally building relationships across the clinical and basic science departments, funded investigators, clinical trials office. A competitive salary, generous benefits, and programmatic and research support will be provided.
THE ENVIRONMENT
Wilmot provides best-in-class cancer treatment and care to approximately three million people in New York State and conducts pivotal research with the goal of preventing and conquering cancer through innovations in science, patient care, education, and community outreach. Wilmot features an 87-bed flagship cancer center, 13 outpatient locations, and one of the state’s largest blood and marrow transplant programs. Wilmot is home to the region’s first cancer survivorship clinic and one of the nation’s first geriatric oncology clinics. Wilmot’s 198 oncology physicians and 514 oncology nurses see more than 7,000 new cancer patients each year. In 2024, Wilmot researchers had $30.9 million in cancer funding, $25.8 million in peer reviewed funding and over $14 million in NCI funding.
URMC and UR Medicine (the clinical enterprise) form the centerpiece of the University’s medical research, teaching, patient care, and community missions. URMC has an integrated administrative structure, budget, and strategic plan. As one of the nation’s leading academic medical centers, URMC ranks among the top quarter of U.S. medical centers in federal research funding, has an overall revenue of approximately $6 billion, and houses the flagship hospital, Strong Memorial Hospital — an 886-bed quaternary care facility. In addition, URMC includes the School of Medicine and Dentistry, School of Nursing, the Golisano Children’s Hospital, Eastman Institute for Oral Health, Sovie Center for Advanced Practice Providers, UR Medical Faculty Group, and UR Medicine comprises seven additional community hospitals.

Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences

jobs.title: Tenured: Professor & Department Head of Microbial Pathogenesis and Immunology
jobs.institution: Texas A&M University: Microbial Pathogenesis and Immunology
jobs.description:
The Department of Microbial Pathogenesis and Immunology (MPIM) at the Texas A&M University Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine (VCOM) seeks to ﬁll one (1) tenured position for a full time, 11-month appointment, with an anticipated start date in the summer or fall of 2027. Applications will be accepted at the rank of tenured Professor, commensurate with qualiﬁcations, and will serve as the Department Head of Microbial Pathogenesis and Immunology.
Mission of the Department: The mission of the MPIM Department is to conduct cutting-edge research to improve human health and to educate the next generation of scientists and clinicians. MPIM has an outstanding track record of innovative scientific achievements in the areas of host-pathogen interactions, virology, bacteriology, and immunology. We are committed to growth in research and scholarship as indicated by sustained and increasing extramural funding and high-impact research.
Strengths of the Department: The MPIM Department offers access to modern research infrastructure, which features open lab design and state-of-the-art research facilities. The Department also houses a BSL-3 facility that accommodates multiple high-consequence pathogens. Additionally, there are excellent vivarium facilities on location, as well as a Laboratory Animal Resources and Research (LARR) facility that provides comprehensive support for in vivo research studies. The Department faculty, students, and staff are supported by updated core facilities, including a flow cytometry and sorting core, an integrated microscopy and imaging core, and a molecular genomics core. The Department is part of a larger research ecosystem within VCOM and other research-intensive Colleges at the University, providing opportunities for interdisciplinary collaborations. The Department enjoys a mix of established, mid-career and new investigators, and is committed to further strengthening the faculty cohort in several key research areas.
Chief Purpose of this Position: We are seeking a renowned scientist in microbial pathogenesis and/or immune responses to infectious agents to serve as Department Head to lead MPIM to future successes. This senior-level faculty position reports to the Dean of the Vashisht College of Medicine and has a key leadership role in this capacity. This individual will lead the department in all academic endeavors, collaborating with both the basic sciences, clinical partners, and other Texas A&M University colleges to oversee the department’s ambitious goals in research, education, and service, as well as manage a rich portfolio of both faculty and department resources.
We seek an individual with a demonstrated track record of academic leadership and expertise in host pathogen interactions, bacteriology, virology, parasitology, mycology, and/or immunology. Individuals working from an interdisciplinary perspective across these themes are especially encouraged to apply.
Position Responsibilities:
1. Research: Collaborate with the faculty to define, develop, and implement a collective vision for the department that engages strategies to expand basic and translational research, and promote commercialization of research discoveries and faculty entrepreneurship.
2. Teaching: Advance the educational mission of the Department, in collaboration with leadership at the Vashisht College of Medicine and Texas A&M University. Facilitate, support, and advocate for the training of the next generation of scientists and physicians who will pioneer future discoveries in microbiology and immunology and deliver exceptional patient care. Champion continuous improvements in medical and graduate education.
3. Service: Provide vision and leadership to advance the reputation of the department, college, and university within the community, state, nation, and beyond. Serve on college and university committees, study sections, academic societies, and as journal editor and/or on editorial boards. Demonstrate a commitment to service within the community. Lead the department to develop and nurture relationships with alumni, donors, and key partners.
4. Administration/Leadership:
a. Leadership: Guide a highly respected microbial pathogenesis and immunology department to the next level of academic excellence. Act as an exemplary role model. Be a highly visible, collaborative leader who supports University and College strategic goals in partnership with other department heads, College academic leaders, and University research leadership. Build a strong and impassioned collaborative vision with department faculty for achieving excellence in all aspects of the academic mission. Understand, appreciate, and prepare for current and future trends in the sciences and help develop a vision for the future of basic science research at the COM. Advocate for faculty and department needs in a highly matrixed academic environment, as a member of the college's leadership team. Nominate members of the department for various internal and external awards and to serve on national committees.
b. Mentorship: Support an environment that mentors and develops all trainees and faculty at all levels (early career, mid-career, and senior). Commit to and actively participate in undergraduate medical and graduate education. Identify, recruit and retain the next generation of superior faculty members. Ensure a supportive atmosphere where research and career development are championed.
c. Administrative and Financial Management: Effectively manage available resources to ensure departmental excellence in administrative processes and procedures. Prepare, oversee, and implement a MPIM departmental budget that encompasses all funding sources and ensures compliance with external grant, legislative, and institutional guidelines. Ensure ethical and fiscally responsible practices within the department.
The Vashisht College of Medicine’s expectations for holding a tenured position include eﬀective graduate and/or medical classroom teaching; mentoring and supervision of graduate and/or medical students and post-doctoral trainees, particularly recruiting and mentoring of doctoral students, including MD/PhD students, and guiding them through graduation in a timely manner; establishment of a vigorous research program sustained through external funding; publication of peer-reviewed research articles that demonstrate impact; and providing service to Texas A&M University and the professional community.
Texas A&M University is one of the highest-ranked public universities in the nation, has a student population of over 80,000 from all 50 states and 124 countries, and is a top 20 research enterprise. Texas A&M University is one of only 24 institutions in the nation to hold the triple designation as a land-grant, sea-grant, and space-grant university. Bryan-College Station has over 275,000 residents, is consistently ranked among the best places to live in the country, has a low cost of living, and is in the heart of the Houston-Dallas-Austin triangle.
Information about Texas A&M University can be found online here: https://www.tamu.edu/about/index.html.
Together, Texas A&M University and the College of Medicine are working to improve healthcare through transformative education, innovative research, and team-based care delivery.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor Position in Advanced Computing, Fall 2026
jobs.institution: The University of Tennessee - Knoxville: Civil & Environ Engr
jobs.description:
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK), invites applications and nominations for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor rank at the intersection of advanced computing and civil and environmental engineering. Candidates should demonstrate a strong record of scholarship, commensurate with career stage, in one or more areas of civil and environmental engineering or in a closely related field with clear relevance to the built or natural environment.
Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, artificial intelligence, machine learning, scientific computing, autonomous and cyber-physical systems, physical AI, high-performance computing, digital twins, and quantum computing. Particular consideration will be given to candidates who develop, adapt, integrate, or rigorously validate advanced computational methods to enable fundamental discovery, predictive modeling, design, decision-making, or autonomous operation in civil and environmental engineering systems. The department seeks candidates whose work extends beyond the routine application of established computational tools and has the potential to produce transformative advances across one or more CEE domains.
The successful candidate will be expected to establish or sustain an externally funded research program and teach undergraduate and graduate courses within their area of expertise. The candidate will also contribute to the development and delivery of interdisciplinary or crossdepartmental curricula in advanced computing, mentor students, and foster collaborations that integrate advanced computational capabilities across CEE research and education.
About the Tickle College of Engineering:
The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE) is in the midst of an unprecedented period of growth and success, including adding over 30 new faculty at all levels to the college over 4 years as part of ambitious hiring campaigns led by Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench. The college has set records in research expenditures, enrollment, incoming student GPA, intellectual property development, and USNWR rank in the past three years. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Lab (ORNL) through the University of Tennessee Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UTORII) and Consolidated Nuclear Security (CNS) that manages the Y-12 National Security Complex have created an expanded opportunity space for faculty and students in the region. New facilities include the state-of-the art Zeanah Engineering Complex, the University of Tennessee Manufacturing and Design Enterprise (TN-MADE) facility, and the Innovation South building that houses UTK’s Fibers and Composites Manufacturing Facility (FCMF), a National Prototype Research Center (NSPC) as part of a partnership with CNS Y-12 under construction, and new facilities for the Biomedical Engineering department and a quantum foundry in planning stages.
TCE currently has 213 tenure/tenure track and over 80 non-tenure track faculty in its nine academic departments and offers 11 undergraduate, 16 MS, and 15 PhD/DE degree programs. Affiliated with TCE and located in Tullahoma, Tennessee, the UT Space Institute is a hub of aerospace and defense research. The college is also home to eight research centers and three interdisciplinary institutes. With approximately 4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students, the college sits 28th among public universities in the most recent U.S. News and World Report graduate rankings. Faculty in the college have won 33 early career awards (NSF, DOE, DARPA, AFOSR, AHA, and Sloan) since 2016. In FY25, the college had annual research expenditures of $113.9M.

The Advanced Practice Provider (ARNP or PA) will be deployed at UWMC and Fred Hutch Cancer Center (FHCC) at the University of Washington Medical Center – Montlake (UWMC-ML) and will provide hematologic/oncologic related evaluation and medical management of patients within the Platinum Service.

Provides care to patients admitted to the hospital for cancer-directed therapy, acute illness, and complications related to therapy, underlying disease, and concurrent illness.
Performs clinical assessment and management of medical needs, performs procedures, participates in goals-of-care discussions, and consults with professional peers working collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team to coordinate care.

The Department of Medicine at Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center (JHBMC) invites applications for the faculty leadership appointment of Medical Director, Department of Medicine Clinical Operations. This leadership role is responsible for advancing the quality, safety, efficiency, and patient-centeredness of inpatient care within the Department of Medicine.
This position provides operational and strategic leadership in partnership with departmental and hospital leadership to support the delivery of high-value clinical care, improve clinical outcomes, and strengthen coordination across care settings. The role is primarily focused on inpatient clinical operations, while also contributing to transitions of care, ambulatory interface opportunities, and alignment with broader population health and institutional initiatives. The Medical Director serves as a key physician leader for Department of Medicine clinical operations and represents the Department in JHBMC and Johns Hopkins Medicine forums as needed.
Faculty Role and Responsibilities
Clinical Operations Leadership
The Medical Director serves as the physician leader for Department of Medicine inpatient operational initiatives and special projects, with primary responsibility for ensuring safe and effective clinical operations. Responsibilities include:
Collaborating with the JHBMC Medical Director of Hospital Capacity to optimize patient flow and bed management within the Department of Medicine
Overseeing bed management throughout the Department of Medicine, including after-hours issues as needed
Monitoring the quality of handoffs and transitions within and between departments
Overseeing quality control for consult services provided by the Department of Medicine
Leading efforts in length-of-stay management, denial reduction, and readmission reduction
Supporting proactive planning for the use of alternate care sites and other utilization strategies
Using data and performance metrics to inform operational decisions and assess the impact of improvement efforts
Monitoring and improving inpatient throughput, including:
Emergency Department decision-to-admit to discharge timing
Discharge and transfer barriers
Supporting physician and staff well-being initiatives
Mentoring and supporting physician leadership development in clinical operations
Supporting improvement in inpatient clinical documentation
Supporting HCAHPS monitoring and improvement efforts
Advancing Department of Medicine and hospital strategic priorities
Developing new models of inpatient care delivery with institutional partners
Refining and implementing collaborative models for inpatient redistribution between JHH and JHBMC campuses
Academic and Institutional Service
In addition to operational responsibilities, this faculty appointment includes active service to departmental and institutional committees and initiatives, including:
DOM Clinical Affairs Practice Meeting (CAPS), held every other week
DOM Clinical Directors Meeting, held monthly
Other internal and hospital operational meetings as required
JHBMC Hospital Capacity Management Committee
Hospital Capacity Committee
Utilization Review Committee, as needed
Medical Board, as needed
Strategic Collaboration
The Medical Director collaborates with institutional leaders to:
Support strategic planning for inpatient clinical services
Enhance access to care and operational efficiency
Develop interdisciplinary approaches to complex patient care
Promote alignment between Department of Medicine operations and hospital objectives
Contribute to clinical initiatives across JHBMC in partnership with hospital leadership
Reporting Structure
This faculty leader reports to the JHBMC Vice President for Medical Affairs and the DOM Vice Chair for Clinical Affairs (VCCA) and indirectly to the Director of the JHBMC Department of Medicine. The Medical Director works collaboratively with the JHBMC DOM Administrator, the JHBMC Medical Director, Capacity, the JHBMC Medical Director, Critical Care Services, DOM Executive Council, Director of the JHBMC Housestaff Residency Program, Director of Nursing for the JHBMC Department of Medicine, and the DOM and JHBMC Manager of Finance
Faculty Expectations
The ideal faculty member for this appointment will be a respected clinician and leader within the Department of Medicine who demonstrates:
Broad understanding of inpatient clinical operations and Department of Medicine mission priorities
Strong leadership, communication, and conflict resolution skills
Emotional intelligence and professionalism in working with faculty, staff, and hospital leadership
Ability to represent the Department effectively in institutional forums
Demonstrated success in collaborative problem-solving and operational improvement
Commitment to patient-centered care, quality, safety, and continuous improvement
Academic Rank, Effort, and Support

Academic rank, percentage effort, and salary support will be determined in accordance with institutional policies, departmental needs, and leadership responsibilities. Based on the vision outlined for the position by the successful candidate, the Medical Director of Department of Medicine Clinical Operations at Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center is estimated to require 25% effort and may be eligible for additional compensation based on performance.

jobs.title: Post-doctoral Fellow - Epidemiology, Traumatic Brain Injury, Brain Aging, and Dementia
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine Postdoctoral
jobs.description:
Dr. Andrea Schneider in the Departments of Neurology and Epidemiology at the University of Pennsylvania is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow to join an NIH-funded research program focused on understanding how traumatic brain injury (TBI) contributes to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) across the life course.
TBI is an important and potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia, yet the mechanisms through which TBI influences long-term cognitive health—and the time course over which these associations emerge—remain poorly understood. This project addresses these critical gaps by leveraging data from more than 40,000 participants from four large, NIH-funded prospective cohort studies: the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health), Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study, Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study, and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). The project uses an accelerated longitudinal/cohort-sequential design and provides an opportunity to work with exceptionally rich longitudinal data spanning adolescence through older adulthood.
The post-doctoral fellow will play a key role in a collaborative research program investigating how cumulative TBI exposure across the life course relates to cognitive trajectories and incident AD/ADRD; how pre- and post-injury vascular risk factors (including hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, smoking, and obesity) modify these associations; and how TBI relates to biomarkers of neurodegeneration and vascular disease.
Open to applications from U.S. citizens and foreign nationals.
Research Opportunities
Depending on the post-doctoral fellow's interests and experience, projects may include:
Harmonizing TBI, cognitive, vascular, biomarker, and neuroimaging measures across large longitudinal cohorts
Examining the relationship between cumulative TBI exposure and long-term cognitive trajectories and dementia risk
Developing novel life-course approaches to understanding the intersection of TBI, vascular disease, brain aging, and AD/ADRD
Developing complementary independent research questions and manuscripts based on the post-doctoral fellow's own scientific interests
Training and Mentorship
The post-doctoral fellow will receive close mentorship in neuroepidemiology, longitudinal epidemiologic methods, life-course epidemiology, dementia epidemiology, biomarker analyses, and analysis of large population-based cohorts. The position is designed to support the post-doctoral fellow's development toward an independent research career, with opportunities to lead publications, present findings at national and international meetings, develop grant applications, and pursue independent research questions.
The fellow will be part of a highly collaborative research environment spanning neurology, epidemiology, biostatistics, neurocritical care, and population health. There will also be opportunities to collaborate with investigators across institutions.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Implementation Science and Dementia Public Health
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: School of Nursing Postdoctoral
jobs.location: Philadelphia, PA (University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing)
jobs.description:
Join the University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing research team as a Postdoctoral Fellow and help state, local and tribal public health programs put proven dementia strategies into practice. The fellow will build and run the implementation science behind the ADRD Public Health Adoption Accelerator (CDC-RFA-DP-26-0227, Component 3): a national registry of which public health sites are taking which Healthy Brain Initiative (HBI) Road Map actions, and a coaching program that helps sites take more of them. The role offers high-impact research with a multidisciplinary team, direct work with health departments and tribal programs across the country, and mentored preparation for an independent research career.
The Postdoctoral Fellow will engage in a range of research activities, primarily focused on:
• Prioritization and Implementation Strategy Registry (35%). The fellow will lead the coding manual and environmental scan that score 30+ BOLD-funded sites against the 24 State and Local Road Map actions or the 13 actions in the Road Map for American Indian and Alaska Native Peoples (coded separately), and maintain the Registry as sites are re-rated over time.
• Coaching strategy and evaluation (30%). Working with the TA coach the fellow will specify tiered coaching (light, standard, intensive) as named implementation strategies (ERIC), design coaching logs, and evaluate coaching dose, fidelity and implementation outcomes.
• Launchpad needs assessment (15%). The fellow will build the baseline rating instrument, code barriers and facilitators using CFIR 2.0, and help tribal partners adapt measures in line with tribal data sovereignty.
• Dissemination (10%). The fellow will lead manuscripts, conference abstracts and practice briefs, including how-to guides for Road Map actions with few existing models.
• 10% - Protected time to conduct and disseminate independent research. Mentorship will be provided to foster the scientist's professional growth, including mentored grant writing toward independence.
Responsibilities:
• Independent review of 30+ BOLD sites for an environmental scan.
• Identify exemplar sites for each Road Map action and load coded data for the Registry launch
• Build the Launchpad baseline needs assessment and summarize site readiness by action.
• Apply implementation frameworks such as CFIR, ERIC, RE-AIM and Proctor's implementation outcomes across the project.
• Maintain the action-by-strategy coaching menu and design coaching logs; analyze coaching dose, fidelity and outcomes.
• Partner with state, local and tribal health department staff, the TA coach and advisory groups to keep tools practical for public health settings; follow tribal protocols and data sovereignty agreements.
• Support day-to-day project administration with Project Director and PI, including timelines, deliverables and compliance with CDC funding requirements.
• Supervise and mentor graduate research assistants who assist with document extraction and coding.
• Manage and analyze qualitative and quantitative data using appropriate software and methods.
• Contribute to conference abstracts and peer-reviewed manuscripts through lead and co-authorship; present at scientific and public health practice meetings.
• Collaborate on the development of external grant proposals.
Position Details:
Approximate Start and End Dates: This is a full-time, fixed-term, grant-funded position expected to run from January 2027 (or when the position is filled) through December 2030, based on the availability of continued grant funding and performance.
Appointment Type: Full-time, fixed-term, grant-funded position.
Location: University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing, Philadelphia, PA. Hybrid options.
Contract and Salary: The annual base salary for this position is $67,000. This is a full-time, fixed-term position for 1 year with potential for renewal based on performance and continued grant funding.
